introduction-cicd-for-kubernetes-by-kube.core: Tekton implements CI/CD as Kubernetes CRDs: each Task runs as a Pod, so pipelines scale with the cluster, use no resources when idle, and use Kubernetes RBAC, secrets and scheduling.

first_principles.problem: A traditional CI server is always on, separately managed and scaled, and isolated from the cluster it deploys to.

analogy.title: A restaurant that hires chefs per order
analogy.story: No standing kitchen staff at 3 AM; chefs appear when an order arrives and leave when it's done.
analogy.breaks: It's very low-level. Many teams use higher-level products built on Tekton (OpenShift Pipelines).

example.title: A build on demand
example.outcome: CI/CD that is just more Kubernetes.

check.q: How does a Tekton Task execute?
check.a: As a Kubernetes Pod, with each step as a container.

the-atomic-units-task-and-taskrun.core: A Task is a reusable template: parameters, workspaces and ordered steps (containers). A TaskRun is one execution of it with concrete values. Steps in a Task share the Pod's volumes.

first_principles.problem: You need reusable, parameterised build units that run predictably.
truths: Steps in a Pod can share files.

analogy.title: A recipe card and a cooking session
analogy.story: The card (Task) lists ingredients and steps; tonight's session (TaskRun) uses specific quantities.
analogy.breaks: Large data shouldn't go through results; use workspaces.

steps.label: Run
steps.detail: A TaskRun references go-test with pkg=./api/...

code.text:
apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
kind: Task
metadata: { name: go-test }
spec:
  params: [ { name: pkg, default: ./... } ]
  workspaces: [ { name: source } ]
  steps:
    - name: test
      image: golang:1.22
      workingDir: $(workspaces.source.path)
      script: go test $(params.pkg)

check.q: Do steps in a Tekton Task run in the same Pod?
check.a: Yes. They run sequentially as containers in one Pod and share its volumes.

orchestration-pipeline-and-pipelinerun.core: A Pipeline wires Tasks into a DAG, using runAfter and data dependencies (results) for order, passing params and workspaces down, with finally tasks for cleanup or notification. A PipelineRun executes it.

first_principles.problem: Build, test, scan and deploy must run in the right order with shared inputs.
truths: Independent tasks can run in parallel.
derivation: Map **pipeline params and workspaces** onto tasks.

analogy.title: A film production schedule
analogy.story: Scenes (Tasks) are scheduled by dependency, some shot in parallel, with a wrap party (finally) whatever happens.
analogy.breaks: Every Task is a new Pod, so data passing costs I/O; design workspaces carefully.

example.title: Clone → test ∥ lint → build

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: test and lint run in parallel, and notify always runs.

example.outcome: complex workflows orchestrated as a DAG.

check.q: What are Tekton finally tasks for?
check.a: Tasks that always run at the end, such as notifications and cleanup, whether the pipeline succeeded or failed.

workspaces-sharing-data-between-pods.core: Each Task is a separate Pod, possibly on a different node, so files are shared through workspaces backed by PersistentVolumeClaims (often via volumeClaimTemplate per run), ConfigMaps or Secrets.

first_principles.problem: The clone Task's source code isn't visible to the test Task running in another Pod.
derivation: Declare **workspaces** in Tasks and the Pipeline.
Bind them in the PipelineRun: **volumeClaimTemplate** (per-run PVC).
Watch **ReadWriteOnce** (pods pinned to one node) vs **RWX**.
Use **secret/configMap** workspaces for credentials and config.

analogy.title: A shared locker between shifts
analogy.story: Each shift worker (Pod) leaves materials in a locker (PVC) for the next.
analogy.breaks: RWO PVCs can force tasks onto one node and limit parallelism.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Each run gets fresh shared storage, deleted with the run.

code.text:
workspaces:
  - name: src
    volumeClaimTemplate:
      spec:
        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
        resources: { requests: { storage: 1Gi } }

check.q: Why can't Tekton Tasks share files through /tmp?
check.a: Each Task runs in its own Pod, possibly on a different node, with a separate filesystem.

triggers-automating-pipeline-execution.core: Tekton Triggers turn incoming events (Git webhooks) into PipelineRuns. An EventListener receives the HTTP event, Interceptors validate and filter it, TriggerBindings extract fields, and TriggerTemplates stamp out the runs.

first_principles.problem: Manually applying PipelineRun YAML for every push isn't CI.
truths: Event payloads contain the needed parameters.

analogy.title: A mailroom that turns letters into work orders
analogy.story: It receives mail, checks it's genuine, extracts the details and issues a standard work order.
analogy.breaks: The EventListener must be exposed to the internet, so validate signatures.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A push to main automatically creates a PipelineRun.

code.text:
kind: TriggerBinding
spec:
  params:
    - { name: revision, value: $(body.after) }
    - { name: repo-url, value: $(body.repository.clone_url) }
---
# EventListener interceptors: github (secretRef), cel filter: body.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

check.q: What role does an Interceptor play in Tekton Triggers?
check.a: It validates (e.g. the webhook signature) and filters or modifies events before they create runs.
